## Learning objectives

By the end you should be able to:

- Define a **random variable**, expectation, and variance.
- Recognize the **distributions** we'll reuse: binomial, Poisson, exponential, geometric.
- Explain what a **stochastic process** is and why evolution is one (drift, mutation).

# Probability building blocks {.center}

## Random variables & expectation

- Sample space, events, probability axioms (placeholder).
- Discrete vs continuous RVs; PMF/PDF/CDF.
- $\mathbb E[X]$, $\mathrm{Var}(X)$; linearity of expectation.
- Law of total probability / conditioning (used in the coalescent derivations).

## The distributions we'll reuse

| Distribution | Models | Shows up in |
|---|---|---|
| **Binomial** | # successes in $n$ trials | Wright–Fisher sampling (popgen 01) |
| **Poisson** | # rare events in an interval | mutations on a branch (popgen 01) |
| **Exponential** | waiting time (continuous) | coalescent / CTMC (popgen, phylo) |
| **Geometric** | waiting time (discrete) | pairwise coalescence (popgen 01) |

# Stochastic processes {.center}

## Evolution is a stochastic process

- A **stochastic process** = a random variable indexed by time.
- **Poisson process** — events at constant rate $\lambda$; interarrival times
  $\sim \text{Exponential}(\lambda)$; counts $\sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda t)$ *(the reading)*.
- **Markov chains** — memoryless state change; the substitution CTMC (phylo) and drift.

::: {.callout-note}
This is the toolbox for the rest of the course: **drift** (binomial sampling), **mutation**
(Poisson), the **coalescent** (exponential waiting times), and **substitution models**
(continuous-time Markov chains). <span class="xref">→ popgen deck 01; phylogenetics theory.</span>
:::

## Summary

- Random variables + a handful of **distributions** describe evolutionary randomness.
- A **Poisson process** links rates, waiting times, and counts.
- Evolutionary genetics = applied stochastic processes. (Develop: add worked probability
  examples / an in-class problem.)
